root_cause.text: The bridge neighbor-suppression path in br_input.c/br_device.c gated IPv6 ND handling with the compile-time check IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) instead of the runtime state ipv6_mod_enabled(), so with ipv6.disable=1 it still executed br_do_suppress_nd() even though the IPv6 neighbor table ipv6_stub->nd_tbl was never initialized.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that with 'ipv6.disable=1' “nd_tbl is never initialized because inet6_init() exits before ndisc_init()” and that “br_do_suppress_nd() will dereference ipv6_stub->nd_tbl which is NULL”; the patch fixes both callers by changing `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` to `ipv6_mod_enabled()` in `net/bridge/br_device.c` and `net/bridge/br_input.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a runtime IPv6 availability check in br_dev_xmit() so IPv6 neighbor suppression runs only when the IPv6 module is enabled.
intent_record.what: The IPv6-related condition in br_dev_xmit() was changed from a compile-time/configuration check using IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) to a runtime/module-availability check using ipv6_mod_enabled().
intent_record.how: This makes the bridge transmit path execute the IPv6 neighbor suppression logic only when IPv6 support is actually enabled at runtime, avoiding incorrect entry into that path when IPv6 is not active despite kernel configuration support being present.

intent_record.what: The conditional guarding the IPv6 neighbor suppression path was changed from a compile-time feature check using IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) to a runtime/module-aware check using ipv6_mod_enabled().
intent_record.how: This makes the bridge frame handling code enter the IPv6-specific suppression logic only when IPv6 support is actually enabled or available at runtime, avoiding reliance solely on kernel build configuration and preventing incorrect execution when IPv6 is not active as a module.

consistency_review.core_intent: Replace the build-time IPv6 guard for bridge neighbor suppression with a runtime IPv6 availability check so the logic only runs when IPv6 support is actually enabled.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they replace compile-time IPv6 checks with a runtime IPv6-enabled check in the bridge neighbor-suppression path, preventing ND suppression from running when IPv6 is disabled and the ND table is uninitialized.

candidates.rationale: This build-time guard is the root cause: it allows the IPv6 ND suppression path to execute whenever IPv6 was compiled in, even if IPv6 was runtime-disabled via ipv6.disable=1, leading to use of uninitialized IPv6 neighbor-table state.

This statement incorrectly gates the IPv6 neighbor-suppression logic on compile-time CONFIG_IPV6 rather than runtime IPv6 availability, so br_do_suppress_nd() can be reached when ipv6_stub->nd_tbl was never initialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional gates the IPv6 neighbor-suppression transmit path using the compile-time CONFIG_IPV6 state instead of runtime IPv6 availability. As a result, the ND suppression logic can run even when IPv6 is disabled via ipv6.disable=1, reaching code that depends on ipv6_stub->nd_tbl being initialized when it is not.

This conditional similarly uses a compile-time IPv6 check to guard the bridge input-side neighbor-suppression path. That allows br_do_suppress_nd() to execute when IPv6 support was compiled in but runtime-disabled, causing access to uninitialized IPv6 neighbor-table state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact IPv6 ND gating logic added in this commit. The vulnerable construct is present in the new branch: `} else if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) && skb->protocol == htons(ETH_P_IPV6) && br->neigh_suppress_enabled && pskb_may_pull(...) && ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr == IPPROTO_ICMPV6) { ... if (msg) br_do_suppress_nd(skb, br, vid, NULL, msg); }`. The root cause says ND suppression must be gated by the runtime state `ipv6_mod_enabled()` rather than the compile-time check `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)`. Here the code uses only `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)` before calling `br_do_suppress_nd()`. Therefore, when IPv6 is compiled in but disabled at runtime (`ipv6.disable=1`), this path could still execute, matching the described vulnerability. No runtime `ipv6_mod_enabled()` check or equivalent fix is present, so the function contains the bug and is not fixed.
